claim: Character count since the last newline is linearly decodable
published: Haiku: probe R² 0.985 after layer 1; open models (T-Tech): Qwen3-8B 0.852 at L5, Gemma-2-9B 0.868
ours: Qwen3-1.7B: best held-out R² 0.747 at layer 6 (shuffled labels -0.005); GPT-2 small 0.759
criterion: Qwen3-1.7B best R² ≥ 0.7 and ≥ 0.5 above the shuffled control

claim: The counts lie on a low-dimensional curved manifold
published: Haiku: top 6 PCs of per-count means hold 95% of variance; helix-like curve with ringing
ours: Qwen3-1.7B layer 6: 6 PCs hold 66% (3 PCs 49%); PC1–2 angle turns 1.93°/char
criterion: 6 PCs ≥ 80% of variance of the per-count means

claim: The count is represented in the very first layers
published: Haiku: R² 0.985 already after layer 1 (T-Tech: early peak not replicated in open models)
ours: Qwen3-1.7B: best R² within layers 0–2 = 0.668 (best overall 0.747 at layer 6)
criterion: early-layer R² ≥ 0.9 × the best layer's R²

claim: The model breaks lines where the text does
published: Haiku predicts newlines at the wrap width (newline probability 0.79 in their example)
ours: AUC of P(newline) for true line breaks: Qwen3-1.7B 0.936, GPT-2 small 0.742
